metadata.title: A Constructive Proof of the General Lovasz Local Lemma (Moser & Tardos, 2009)
metadata.framework: Algorithmic constructive proof of the Lovasz Local Lemma via a simple resample-based algorithm with entropy compression analysis
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on arXiv:0903.0544 PDF text.

nodes.name: Lovasz Local Lemma (LLL) setting
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{P} = \{P_1, \ldots, P_n\}$ be a finite set of mutually independent random variables. Let $\mathcal{A} = \{A_1, \ldots, A_m\}$ be a collection of 'bad' events, each determined by a subset $\mathrm{vbl}(A_i) \subseteq \mathcal{P}$ of the variables. The dependency graph $G = (\mathcal{A}, E)$ has an edge $(A_i, A_j)$ whenever $\mathrm{vbl}(A_i) \cap \mathrm{vbl}(A_j) \neq \emptyset$. Let $\Gamma(A_i)$ denote the neighborhood of $A_i$ in $G$.

nodes.name: LLL condition (symmetric form)
nodes.statement: The symmetric LLL condition states: if each event $A_i$ has $\Pr[A_i] \leq p$ and each event depends on at most $d$ other events (i.e., $|\Gamma(A_i)| \leq d$), then $epd \leq 1$ implies $\Pr[\bigcap_i \overline{A_i}] > 0$. The general (asymmetric) form: if there exist $x_i \in (0,1)$ such that $\Pr[A_i] \leq x_i \prod_{A_j \in \Gamma(A_i)} (1 - x_j)$ for all $i$, then $\Pr[\bigcap_i \overline{A_i}] > 0$.

nodes.name: Moser-Tardos resample algorithm
nodes.statement: Sample all variables $P_1, \ldots, P_n$ independently from their distributions. While there exists a violated event $A_i$ (i.e., $A_i$ holds under the current assignment): select an arbitrary violated event $A_i$; resample all variables in $\mathrm{vbl}(A_i)$ independently from their original distributions. Output the final assignment.

nodes.name: Termination and efficiency of the Moser-Tardos algorithm
nodes.statement: If the LLL condition holds with witnesses $x_i \in (0,1)$ satisfying $\Pr[A_i] \leq x_i \prod_{A_j \in \Gamma(A_i)} (1 - x_j)$, then the Moser-Tardos algorithm terminates after an expected number of resamplings at most $\sum_{i=1}^{m} \frac{x_i}{1 - x_i}$. In the symmetric case $epd \leq 1$, this gives $O(m/d)$ expected resamplings.

nodes.name: Proof via witness trees / entropy compression
nodes.statement: The proof assigns each resampling step a witness tree: a rooted tree whose root is the resampled event and whose children represent causally related previous resamplings. Key insight: each witness tree is a Galton-Watson-type random structure. The expected number of occurrences of any fixed witness tree $\tau$ with root $A_i$ is at most $\prod_{A_j \in \tau} \frac{x_j}{1 - x_j}$. Summing over all possible witness trees (which form a tree-indexed family) and using the LLL condition to bound the generating function gives the total bound.

nodes.name: Constructive LLL
nodes.statement: Under the LLL conditions, there exists a randomized polynomial-time algorithm that finds an assignment avoiding all bad events $A_1, \ldots, A_m$ with probability 1 (Las Vegas algorithm). This makes the LLL fully constructive.

nodes.name: Simplicity compared to prior constructive approaches
nodes.statement: Prior constructive versions of LLL (Beck 1991, Alon 1991, Molloy-Reed 1998, Czumaj-Scheideler 2000) required increasingly complex conditions and algorithms. The Moser-Tardos algorithm is strikingly simple: just resample any violated event. The proof that it works under the full LLL conditions is also elegant.

nodes.name: Parallel version
nodes.statement: A parallel version of the algorithm resamples all independent violated events simultaneously, achieving $O(\log^2 m)$ parallel rounds under the LLL conditions. This gives an efficient RNC algorithm for all LLL applications.

nodes.name: k-SAT application
nodes.statement: For a $k$-SAT formula where each variable appears in at most $2^k/(ek)$ clauses, the LLL guarantees a satisfying assignment exists. The Moser-Tardos algorithm finds one efficiently: resample variables of any unsatisfied clause until all clauses are satisfied.
